result.reviewScopeSummary: Reviewed Story 1 against the story spec, full Epic 5 tech design, and test plan; then inspected the new turn-projection service, token-count wiring, prepare-mode catch-up path, and the current runtime lower-band selection/materialization surfaces, followed by running both verification gates.

newFindings.title: Conversation-only turn projections are still isolated to direct service tests and never enter the real lower-band runtime path
newFindings.evidence: `rg -n "ensureLowerBandTurnProjection" src tests` returns only the service definition at `src/thread/async-thread/services/lower-band-turn-projection-service.ts:515` and direct calls from `tests/thread/lower-band-turn-projection-service.test.ts`; there is no production caller. The actual prepare path in `src/thread/async-thread/services/async-thread-run-service.ts:590-842` and `:920-1038` still validates and repairs only `turn.smooth`, `chunk.smoothText`, and `chunk.placeholders`, then runs `ensureSmoothTurn()`, `updateChunkState()`, and `ensurePlaceholderArtifacts()`. The builder/materializer also still consume placeholder artifacts in `src/thread-view/services/thread-view-builder.ts:304-340` and `src/thread-view/services/thread-view-materializer.ts:418-524`. As shipped, closed turns do not produce or reuse `turn.smooth.lowerBandProjection` in any production workflow, and projection-count failure cannot block lower-band chunk/readiness decisions.

productionPathFindings: No production caller invokes `ensureLowerBandTurnProjection`; the symbol is only referenced by its direct service tests and its own definition.

Prepare/build/materialization still route lower-band behavior through `chunk.placeholders` and `smoothText` (`async-thread-run-service.ts`, `thread-view-builder.ts`, `thread-view-materializer.ts`), so the real conversation-only projection path is not active in the app/runtime.
additionalObservations: `npm run verify` and `npm run verify-all` both passed.
Service-level coverage is strong for deterministic formatting, exclusion rules, user-only turns, reopen reuse, exact counter failure, stale-writer protection, and stderr warnings.
The passing gates do not cover the blocking gap because the new projection service is exercised directly in its own tests rather than through a production prepare/build flow.
